**No improvement in reaching the known solutions on these harder cases.**
Ordinary ML and direct PSD recover exactly the same targets with normalization
off and on. Two-stage PSD loses three targets in the later batch: two fits
exhaust their budgets and one reaches a worse local solution. This run supports
normalization as a numerical scaling tool, not a remedy for missed solutions.

**Follow-up:** the [two-stage investigation](two-stage-summary.html) isolates
handoff sensitivity. More iterations do not rescue the lost targets; a stricter
handoff rule gains two targets but loses one across all 120 draws. No policy
change is adopted.

## The important data

**Targets reached: normalization off → on.** Each row contains 20 saved datasets.
ML has 19 eligible targets in each weak-marker row because one known near-pole
case is kept separate; all other rows/methods have 20 targets.

```{r}
x <- read.csv("results/normalization-revisit/by_family.csv")
a <- x[x$arm=='original_units',]; b <- x[x$arm=='normalized',]
p <- merge(a,b,by=c('batch','design','method'),suffixes=c('_off','_on'))
k <- expand.grid(design=c('ernst','weak_marker','high_r2'),batch=c('development','fresh'),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
t <- data.frame(Batch=ifelse(k$batch=='development','Earlier','Later'),
                Problem=unname(c(ernst='Ernst',weak_marker='Weak markers',high_r2='High R²')[k$design]))
for(m in c('ml_lbfgs','ml_port','direct_psd','two_stage_psd')) {
 z <- p[p$method==m,]; z <- z[match(paste(k$batch,k$design),paste(z$batch,z$design)),]
 t[[switch(m,ml_lbfgs='ML: L-BFGS',ml_port='ML: PORT',direct_psd='Direct PSD',two_stage_psd='Two-stage PSD')]] <-
 paste0(z$target_reached_off,' → ',z$target_reached_on)
}
knitr::kable(t,row.names=FALSE)
```

A target is a saved best-observed solution, not a proven global optimum. A hit
requires a matching objective, the library convergence verdict, requested-marker
accuracy, and the study chart check; PSD also requires admissibility. The old
magnitude cutoff is not used to reject finite solutions here.

## The difficult cases are still difficult

- **Seven refined finite ML solutions:** L-BFGS reaches **one of seven** and
  PORT **two of seven**, unchanged. Six saved solutions still pass accuracy
  when checked directly; the exceptionally flat minimum with loading about
  **740** remains ill-conditioned. The other misses cannot all be dismissed
  as nonexistent solutions.
- **Two expected chart failures:** neither produces a certified ML fit in this
  rerun. Their saved near-pole endpoints still fail the explicit study chart
  tolerance of 1e-4, including the loading around **184,000**. The library's
  1e-6 translation tolerance still admits both saved endpoints; a general
  production rejection policy remains unfinished.
- **Later-batch PSD:** direct PSD stays at **47/60** targets; two-stage drops
  **49 → 46/60**. The losses are Ernst, N=20, draws 1 and 3, and high-R²,
  N=20, draw 7. Draw 3 reaches objective 0.403856 instead of 0.391933;
  the other two exhaust the PSD evaluation budget.

**Next:** investigate those two-stage regressions and the missed finite
solutions. Scaling alone has not solved the start/solution-search problem.
Spectral alternatives remain banked; this run neither adds multistart nor
changes markers automatically.

**Scope:** these are the earlier simulated sphere challenges, not textbook
corpus models: 120 datasets, four methods, two normalization settings =
**960 fits**. ML uses layered/native starts, L-BFGS or PORT with information
scaling. PSD uses FABIN3/auto and SLSQP with diagonal preconditioning; two-stage
first tries L-BFGS. Budgets are 5,000 evaluations, relative objective tolerance
1e-12 and parameter tolerance 1e-10. Both arms use the same current judge.
Saved references never enter the starts. Both batches are development data.
